description:
Vital Recorder 1.16.6 is open on the Windows desktop in Track mode with the file '0001.vital' from the VitalDB open dataset loaded. The track window shows multiple waveform traces from a noncardiac surgery at Seoul National University Hospital, including arterial pressure (ART, red), ECG leads (ECG_II, ECG_V5, green), pulse oximetry (PLETH, light blue), capnography (CO2, yellow), and airway pressure (AWP, white). The toolbar at the top-left shows six icon buttons, and the event panel on the right shows surgical event timestamps.

Vital Recorder has two display modes:
- Track mode (current): Shows all waveform traces over time in a scrollable track window with a timeline at the top
- Monitor mode: Shows numeric vital signs values in large-format display panels, similar to a bedside patient monitor, with only a minimal waveform strip

Your task:
1. Switch the display from Track mode to Monitor mode. The toggle button is the first icon in the top-left toolbar area (it looks like a small monitor/signal display icon).
2. After switching, the display should change dramatically: instead of multiple waveform tracks, you should see large numeric value displays (such as BIS, BT/body temperature) and a single minimal waveform strip, resembling a bedside patient monitor screen.
